work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'The Words of the Griot Mamadou Kouyaté,' p. 1; 'Nana Triban and Balla Fasséké,' pp. 56-58; John William Johnson, Son-Jara: The Mande Epic Performance by Jeli Fa-Digi Sisòkò · publication description
literal_gloss: specialist oral performer/historian; English 'griot' is not an exact equivalent
definition: The Niane/Pickett framing calls Mamadou Kouyaté and Balla Fasséké 'griots'; the role carries hereditary, historical, genealogical, musical, and patronage relations in Mande contexts.
cultural_caution: Do not reduce jeli to a fantasy bard, a generic storyteller, or a caste/class mechanic. Roles, terminology, and authority vary by language, lineage, performance, and social context.

citations.locator: 'The Words of the Griot Mamadou Kouyaté,' p. 1; 'Nana Triban and Balla Fasséké,' pp. 56-58

supports: Jeli Fa-Digi Sisòkò performance and Mandekan oral-performance context.

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'The First Kings of Mali,' pp. 2-3; 'The Buffalo Woman,' pp. 4-11
definition: The witness's opening genealogy labels several named forebears Simbon and calls Mamadi Kani a hunter king; named hunters initiate the Sogolon episode.
cultural_caution: This functional map does not turn Mande hunting knowledge, ritual, or social identity into a generic ranger class.

citations.locator: 'The First Kings of Mali,' pp. 2-3; 'The Buffalo Woman,' pp. 4-11

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'Kouroukan Fougan or The Division of the World,' pp. 73-78; 'Niani,' pp. 79-82
definition: The Pickett translation repeatedly presents Sundiata and other rulers in kingship language, including the title Mansa at the Kouroukan Fougan settlement.
cultural_caution: The workbook's 'Warlord Ruler' is only an analytic comparison; it neither defines Mande sovereignty nor supports a claim that rule rested solely on conquest.

citations.locator: 'Kouroukan Fougan or The Division of the World,' pp. 73-78; 'Niani,' pp. 79-82
supports: Mansa/kingship framing in the declared witness.

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'The Buffalo Woman,' pp. 4-11; 'Exile,' pp. 26-37
literal_gloss: foretelling and destined future in this translation
definition: An unnamed Hunter-Soothsayer foretells Sundiata's future kingship; later chapters repeatedly frame the hero's path as destiny.
cultural_caution: This is a translation-level narrative descriptor, not a reconstructed Mandekan technical term or evidence of a uniform magical system.

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'Exile,' pp. 26-37; 'The Return,' pp. 47-53
definition: The chapter titled 'Exile' follows Sogolon, Sundiata, and their kin leaving Niani; the return structures the later campaign.
cultural_caution: The archetype is a comparative plot label, not an equivalence claim about Mande displacement, kinship, or political legitimacy.

supports: Exile and return sequence in this witness.

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'Soumaoro Kanté: The Sorcerer King,' pp. 38-39; 'History,' pp. 40-42; 'Krina,' pp. 59-69
definition: The witness styles Soumaoro a 'Sorcerer King' and links his extraordinary power to jinn; it also attributes specialized knowledge to other figures.
cultural_caution: Do not infer a single Mande category of 'magic,' an innate fantasy sorcerer class, or an ethnographic account of ritual practice from this literary translation label.

citations.locator: 'Soumaoro Kanté: The Sorcerer King,' pp. 38-39; 'History,' pp. 40-42; 'Krina,' pp. 59-69
supports: Sorcery/jinn framing in the declared witness.

work_or_witness: Epic of Sundiata · David Schoenbrun, 'Gendered Themes in Early African History,' pp. 263-264
literal_gloss: mother-childness; solidarity among uterine kin (scholarly gloss)
definition: A scholarly Mande kinship term useful for cautiously contextualizing Sogolon's children and their mutual support in exile; it is not a word supplied by the Pickett translation at those scenes.
cultural_caution: Use as scholarly context, not as a universal rule, game bond, or unqualified explanation of every family action in this witness.

citations.locator: David Schoenbrun, 'Gendered Themes in Early African History,' pp. 263-264
supports: Badenya as mother-childness and solidarity; Sunjata/exile context.

work_or_witness: Epic of Sundiata · David Schoenbrun, 'Gendered Themes in Early African History,' pp. 263-264
literal_gloss: father-childness; rivalry/competition among paternal kin (scholarly gloss)
definition: A scholarly Mande kinship term that can cautiously contextualize the witness's succession conflict between Sundiata and his paternal half-brother Dankaran Touman; it is not a witness-level total explanation.
cultural_caution: Do not treat fadenya as an ethnic stereotype, deterministic family law, or a fantasy rivalry mechanic.

citations.locator: David Schoenbrun, 'Gendered Themes in Early African History,' pp. 263-264

work_or_witness: D. T. Niane, Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali · 'Kouroukan Fougan or The Division of the World,' pp. 73-78
literal_gloss: rendered in this witness as 'The Division of the World'
definition: The witness names a post-victory settlement in which Sundiata distributes kingdoms and offices; it is a founding narrative episode in this text.
cultural_caution: Do not collapse this chapter into a timeless constitution, a complete historical legal code, or a generic kingdom-building mechanic; its form and significance vary across sources and modern uses.

citations.locator: 'Kouroukan Fougan or The Division of the World,' pp. 73-78
